exposure: need for admission to Intensive Care Unit
birth with less than 37 weeks of gestation
having a dead sibling aged less than 5 years old
mother did not undergo prenatal care
outcome: cumulative prevalence of biological and social risk factors at birth
classification of newborns into usual risk or at-risk categories
cohort: The study included 4,480 live births in a medium-sized city in Brazil between January 2018 and July 2020.
finding: The study found that 21.1% of newborns were classified as at risk, with most presenting more than one risk factor, and the biological risk rate was 7.39 times higher than the social risk rate.
